topics.description: French politician and president of France since 2017 who founded En Marche! and won reelection in 2022.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This leader’s government urged nationals to leave Iran after a couple was accused of inciting protests for its secret service. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this leader of En Marche, who was accused of hypocrisy by Iran for his management of the Yellow Vests protests. This president defeated Marine Le Pen to win re-election in 2022.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Macron showed solidarity for protests over the September 2022 death of this woman. This woman fell into a coma after being detained by Iran’s “morality police.”
parts.answer: ANSWER: Mahsa Amini [accept either underlined portion]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Mahsa Amini was arrested for improperly wearing one of these pieces of clothing, which are mandatory for Iranian women. Marine Le Pen advocated for a nationwide ban of these Islamic headscarves.

parts.label: L
parts.question: When asked how to find a job, this leader of En Marche! once said “cross the street. I’ll find you something.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this politician being investigated by NUPES for his links to lobbying after the release of the “Uber Files.” This politician defeated Marine Le Pen for a second term in his current position.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During the 2022 elections, Macron condemned Le Pen for her proposal to ban these objects in public, saying it would “divide the country.” These headcoverings, often worn by Muslim women, are less restrictive than burkas.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] Macron is currently the president of this country. Yellow vest protesters stormed this country’s capital of Paris to demand social justice.

topics.description: Scottish military leader and Guardian of Scotland who led resistance against Edward I of England and was defeated at the Battle of Falkirk.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Mamluks forced this ruler to retire from Crusading by having him stabbed with an allegedly poisoned  dagger. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this English king, nicknamed “Longshanks,” who won the Battle of Falkirk.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] At the Battle of Falkirk, Edward defeated this rebel leader depicted in Braveheart. This leader was not actually  sold out by Robert the Bruce prior to the Battle of Stirling Bridge.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] After winning the Battle of Falkirk, Edward was nicknamed the “Hammer of” these people. Robert the Bruce  was a king of these people, who name a country north of England.
parts.answer: Scots (or the Hammer of the Scots; or Scotland)

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country traces its earliest monarchies back to Kenneth McAlpin. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country, now a constituent country of the United Kingdom. This country had monarchs that included William the Lion and Robert the Bruce.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The historical boundary between Scotland and England follows one of these structures commissioned by the Roman Emperor Hadrian. One of these structures inspired by that one is built out of ice in Game of Thrones.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Scotland was conquered in the early 1300s by Edward I of England, the Hammer of the Scots. This man was appointed as the Guardian of Scotland to lead the rebellion against Edward I, though he resigned after losing at the Battle of Falkirk.

topics.description: Israeli politician, longtime Likud leader, and multiple-term prime minister who faced corruption and bribery charges while in office.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Cases 1000 and 2000 are corruption and bribery cases brought against a leader in this country. A party in this country founded in 2019 which is led by a former army chief of staff is named after the colors of this country's flag. Another party in this country which is led by Mansour Abbas and holds only four seats in the legislature was the last to join a 2021 electoral coalition. In 2021, (*) Naftali Bennett was sworn in as this country’s prime minister in the fourth election in two years. This country’s parliament, the Knesset, was long controlled by the Likud party. For 10 points, name this country which was led from 2009 to 2021 by Benjamin Netanyahu.
parts.answer: Israel [or State of Israel or Medinat Yisra’el]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A leader of this country asked the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth to hire more favorable journalists in exchange for a law that would hurt a competing paper. An alliance of the Yamina and Yesh Atid parties ousted this country’s prime minister as he was on trial for bribery and fraud. (*) Likud leader Benjamin Netanyahu once led, for ten points, what Middle Eastern country that claims the Palestinian territories of the West Bank and Gaza Strip?
parts.answer: Israel (accept State of Israel; accept Medinat Yisrael)

topics.description: The ancient Roman civilization, including the cultural and political traditions associated with the Roman Republic and Roman Empire.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This civilization celebrated the husband of Ops in a festival which is preceded by "Io" [Yo] in a common greeting. A festival from this civilization involved the election of a mock king and the reversal of master and slave roles. That festival from this civilization celebrated a deity who carried a (*) sickle and was frequently associated with the Greek Cronus. For 10 points, name this civilization, which celebrated Saturnalia in the Forum.

topics.description: British archaeologist who led the 1922 excavation that discovered Tutankhamun’s tomb in Egypt’s Valley of the Kings.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: DNA testing of this man’s mother, “The Younger Lady,” in KV35 proved this man was born from an incestous marriage. Arthur Conan Doyle suggested Lord Carnavon’s death was caused by “elementals” produced by this man’s priests. Howard Carter discovered this man and his (*) gold death mask in the Valley of the Kings in Thebes. For 10 points, name this pharaoh who died young, and whose tomb was discovered remarkably intact.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: DNA analysis has confirmed that this ruler’s mother is KV-35-YL, also called the Younger Lady. This final monarch of the Eighteenth Dynasty abolished his father’s unpopular worship of (*) Aten. This ruler came to power at the age of nine, shortly after the death of Akhenaten, and died at the age of eighteen. For ten points, name this boy pharaoh whose tomb and elaborate, golden death mask were discovered in the Valley of the Kings by Howard Carter.

topics.description: The 1939 nonaggression agreement between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union whose secret protocols divided parts of Eastern Europe into spheres of influence.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country had its eastern border set at the Curzon Line during the Yalta Conference. This country was partitioned three separate times during the 19th century, and was the largest country divided by the secret Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Nazi (*) Germany invaded this country on September 1st, 1939 to start World War II, and the USSR soon followed. For ten points, name this Eastern European country whose capital is Warsaw.
parts.answer: Poland [or the Republic of Poland or Rzeczpospolita Polska]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader persecuted Jews in his country as retribution for the supposed “Doctors’ Plot.” This leader’s forced collectivization policies led to the Holodomor famine in Ukraine. This leader signed a nonaggression pact with (*) Nazi Germany, which Germany broke when they invaded this leader's country in 1941. For 10 points, name this man who led the Soviet Union during World War II, the successor of Vladimir Lenin.
parts.answer: Joseph Stalin [or Ioseb Besarionis dze Jughashvili]

topics.description: Hammurabi was the eighteenth-century BCE king of Babylon best known for his conquests and the Code of Hammurabi, an early surviving written legal code.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A black stele from this city depicts a seated king of this city conversing with Shamash. For a seventy-year period, the Jews were held in a “captivity” named for this city by its king Nebuchadnezzar II. A law code originating the phrase (*) “an eye for an eye” was inscribed on a stele by this city’s king Hammurabi. For 10 points, what ancient Mesopotamian city was once home to The Hanging Gardens?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: In this city, the Etemenanki Temple and the Ishtar Gate were constructed by King Nebuchadnezzar. After a ruler of this city destroyed Solomon's Temple, the Jews suffered a namesake (*) "captivity" in this city. Legal principles like "an eye for an eye" were established in this city by its ruler Hammurabi. For 10 points, name this Mesopotamian city home to some legendary Hanging Gardens.

topics.description: The July 1794 political coup that overthrew Maximilien Robespierre and ended the Reign of Terror and radical Jacobin ascendancy during the French Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the French Revolutionary Calendar, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Holidays celebrating Talent and Labor after the end of Fructidor were named for this umbrella term for lower-class French revolutionaries who wore trousers instead of bourgeois knee-britches.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This summer month of the calendar names an event in which the Directory usurped the power of the Committee of Public Safety and Maximilien Robespierre, thus ending the Reign of Terror.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The decimalized calendar was introduced to weaken the power of the Catholic Church by replacing this other calendar, the most widely used today. This calendar named for a pope replaced the Julian calendar.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This leader used his newspaper, The Defender of the Constitution, to criticize calls for a war against Austria made by Jacques-Pierre Brissot. Cecile Renault attempted to assassinate this leader, who opposed both the Girondists and an atheist cult created by Jacques-René Hebert. This leader promoted the (*) Cult of the Supreme Being and secured power after the death of his former ally Georges Danton. The Thermidorian Reaction began with the execution of this leader and “incorruptible” member of the Committee of Public Safety. For 10 points, name this Jacobin French revolutionary leader who oversaw the Reign of Terror until his own execution by guillotine.

topics.description: A U.S.-sponsored post–World War II economic aid program that supported the recovery of Western European countries.

parts.label: L
parts.question: One holder of this office under Franklin Roosevelt said it wasn’t worth a “bucket of warm spit.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this office, holders of which under FDR included John Garner and Henry A. Wallace. This position is called in to break ties in the Senate and is first in line to succeed the president.
parts.answer: Vice President of the United States [accept VP]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This politician had no vice president during his first term as president, but ran with Alben W. Barkley for his second term. This politician served as FDR’s last vice president, and succeeded him after his death.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] FDR’s former VP Henry A. Wallace opposed this plan, which Truman passed as president. This plan, named after the Secretary of State at the time, had the US give foreign aid to Western Europe to recover after World War II.
parts.answer: Marshall Plan [accept European Recovery Program or ERP; do not accept or prompt on “European Economic Recovery Plan”]

topics.description: Hadrian was a Roman emperor from 117 to 138 CE associated with the suppression of the Bar Kokhba revolt and the construction of Hadrian's Wall.

parts.label: L
parts.question: A revolt of members of this religious group ended with a mass suicide in the Masada fort. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name this oft-persecuted religious group that led multiple revolts against Roman rule. This religious group preceded Christianity and Islam as the first Abrahamic religion.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] During the reign of this emperor, the siege of the Masada ended the First Jewish Revolt. This emperor is said to have fiddled during the Great Fire of Rome.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Simon Bar Kokhba led another major Jewish revolt during the reign of this Roman emperor, who named a defensive wall south of the Antonine Wall that separates Scotland and England.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Name the following brutal ancient Roman emperors, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: This third Emperor of Rome was particularly cruel in treating his underlings and was accused of numerous insane acts, such as his plan to make his own horse a consul.
parts.answer: Caligula (accept Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, but do not prompt on any partial answers thereof)

parts.label: B
parts.question: This ruler ordered the death of his own mother, Agrippina, in 59 CE, five years before he supposedly “fiddled” while the Great Fire of Rome burned on.
parts.answer: Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus (do not accept or prompt on any of the non-underlined names if given alone)

parts.label: C
parts.question: The Bar Kokhba revolt in Judea was suppressed by this emperor, who ordered the construction of a wall along the northern border of Roman Britain in 122 CE.
parts.answer: Hadrian (accept Caesar Traianus Hadrianus, but do not prompt on any partial answers thereof; accept Hadrian’s Wall)
